answer: A defense is bonded work history. Before an agent can take high-value jobs, it must post a refundable stake and build a signed record of completed work, each delivery added like a quill entry in a tamper-evident ledger. New identities start on a low mesa of trust with small, low-paying tasks and slow promotion, while a cedar-like reputation grows only through sustained, verifiable service. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and do real work for each, turning a cheap flood of identities into an expensive, slow operation.
